thread:
mike: noticing a ~18% drop in tokens/sec on prod after the 3.9.1 rollout. surfaced by the usage SLO dashboards.
mike: spike in queue depth in the continuous batcher + CPU on CPU-bound kernel paths. link: https://ci.internal/redwood/prof/2065439876
sophia: ugh. is this the kernel-selection commit from yesterday? @jen landed the heuristic tweak iirc.
jen: yep i merged #5123 (kernel-routing: prefer fp16-kernel for short sequences). changed fallback ordering.
raj: ran a quick git bisect this morning — points at the merge-base around commit 9f2a3b. will drop output in a sec.
perf-bot: CI perf check failed on e2e-regression (tokens/sec -16% vs baseline). details: https://ci.internal/redwood/build/9271
liz: holding the rest of the rollout? production alerts are noisy but not yet paging.
mike: holding. traffic split turned from 100% -> 0% for canary at 09:17.
sophia: raj — can you paste the flamegraphs? also want per-kernel invocation counts and KV cache hit rate.
raj: flamegraph snippet:
```
continuous_batcher::enqueue (wall 210ms)
kernel_dispatch::select_fp16_short (wall 120ms)
kernel_exec::fp16_short (wall 60ms)
kv_cache::fetch_miss (wall 30ms)
```
raj: KV cache miss rate jumped from 6% -> 28% for the affected workload (hot prefix churn).
mike: that explains extra full-token passes. but why smaller batches? queue depth shows lots of small drains.
jen: the heuristic swap lowers the batching window for sequences <64 to avoid padding cost — maybe it shortened the window too aggressively.
sophia: could be interacting with the new startup drain timer we added in the scheduler (PR #5102). timer + shorter window -> suboptimal coalescing.
raj: quick profiler (top-lines):
```
# samples
sched::drain_check  42%
kernel_dispatch   28%
kv_cache_fetch    15%
memcopy           10%
```
raj: also seeing memcopy spikes when we fall back between kernels — extra memcpy to transpose tensors.
liz: perf-bot also flagged a regression in mem bandwidth on the GPU hosts in the canary pool.
mike: actionable items: revert kernel ordering change or tweak batching window + add regression test. thoughts?
jen: willing to revert the kernel-ordering change for now. we should also add a micro-e2e that simulates hot-prefix churn.
sophia: prefer tweak first (less risky) — increase minimum batch window to 6ms and keep kernel-change behind a flag.
raj: bisect log: last good 9e7b4d, bad 9f2a3b (matches jen's merge). attaching the small script I used: `./scripts/bisect_perf.sh --metric tokens_per_sec --range 9e7b4d..9f2a3b`
mike: can we get a controlled replay of the failing trace to test the tweak? link to trace store: https://traces.internal/redwood/2026/03/18/2065438000
liz: i'll provision a canary with revert and run 30m replay. that should give us a clear delta.
perf-bot: scheduled: revert-kernel-ordering on canary-3 at 10:05 UTC. will report back after 30m.
jen: pushing a toggle now so we can flip quickly if revert is too heavy. PR coming up.
sophia: add a telemetry counter for "small_batch_rate" (batches <4) so we can alert before tokens/sec dips.
mike: good idea. also add a kv_cache_miss_ratio metric per model-route. current dashboards aggregate across models and hide hotspots.
raj: note: when kv miss ratio >20% the cost of kernel swap + memcpy kills batching benefits. we should fail open to fp32-kernel for those hot routes.
liz: will monitor. running replay with revert now.
perf-bot: replay 10m mark: tokens/sec delta +12% on reverted canary vs broken canary.
mike: ok revert looked good — rolling back the kernel-ordering merge in prod. keep the batching-window tweak and add telem.
jen: filed PR to revert (link: https://git.internal/redwood/pull/5142) and feature-flag PR here: https://git.internal/redwood/pull/5143
sophia: follow-ups: add micro-e2e, telemetry, and a CI perf job that replays representative hot-prefix traces.
mike: thanks all. new incident ticket: PERF-2026 with action items. will update when postmortem draft is ready.
liz: thumbs up :thumbsup:
raj: adding flamegraphs and bisect logs into the ticket.
perf-bot: incident ticket PERF-2026 created at https://incidents.internal/redwood/2026/PERF-2026
mike: closing thread here, will ping when postmortem is live.
